extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: Vibravox is a GDPR-compliant dataset containing audio recordings captured with five different body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) alongside an airborne microphone reference. It contains over 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded from 188 participants across clean and 3D spatialized noisy acoustic conditions.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, Éric Bavu
extraction.citeAs: J. Hauret, M. Olivier, C. Langrenne, S. Poirée, and É. Bavu, "vibravox (revision 071945b)," 2024. [Online]. Available: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Cnam-LMSSC/vibravox
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Participants were equipped with six audio sensors (an airborne headset microphone, a forehead accelerometer, a soft in-ear microphone, a rigid in-ear microphone, a throat microphone, and a temple vibration pickup) connected to a Zoom F8n field recorder sampling simultaneously at 48 kHz and 32 bits. Data collection was divided into four consecutive recording steps per participant: speech-clean (15 minutes of reading French Wikipedia sentences in quiet), speechless-noisy (2 minutes 24 seconds of silence in a 56-loudspeaker 3D spatializer playing AudioSet ambient noise), speechless-clean (54 seconds of silence capturing physiological and sensor noise), and speech-noisy (54 seconds of reading in 3D spatialized noise from concert and street recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Direct measurement, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A small number of audio clips had shortcomings due to mispronounced sentences, sensors shifting position, occasional sensor malfunctions, or instances where a microphone was inadvertently left unequipped. An automated filtering pipeline excluded 12 participants and 6.8% of pronounced utterances, retaining 188 out of 200 participants and 28,471 sentences out of 30,568 collected.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reading text sourced from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice; ambient noises sourced from AudioSet and in-house ambisonic recordings of concerts and street events; audio signals directly measured from human participants.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A 20 Hz high-pass filter was uniformly applied to each acquisition channel during recording to attenuate low-frequency noise and artifacts. Following post-processing filtering, timestamps generated by Voice Activity Detection (VAD) were extended by 0.6 seconds on both ends, and audio was trimmed by 15 ms on segment boundaries when timestamps exceeded original bounds to eliminate edge artifacts such as mouse clicks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Textual data was normalized (lowercased, punctuation removed except apostrophes) and filtered to exclude numerals, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, syntactic errors, and most proper names (retaining only common first names, French town/region names, and country names). Recorded speech-clean audio was filtered based on three automatic criteria: Phoneme Error Rate (PER) < 10% computed using whisper-timestamped and Levenshtein distance, SNR > 1.5 dB, and speech sound level exceeding silence sound level (Lspeech_50 > Lsilence_50).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Phonetic transcriptions based on the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA, 33 French phonemes) were automatically generated using the text phonemizer of the CoML lab, followed by manual phonetic transcription for unrecognized words (such as 'algorithme'). Word timestamps and voiced/silent speech segments were produced using the whisper-timestamped speech-to-text tool.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Audio samples exhibiting a Phoneme Error Rate (PER) greater than 10% relative to Whisper predictions were filtered out to eliminate discrepancies between labeled text and actual participant pronunciation. Language switches produced by the phonemizer were manually identified and transcribed to preserve a minimal 33-phoneme French phonetic alphabet.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Participant voice recordings (biometric data), gender (Female/Male), and age (ranging from 18 to 82 years, with mean and median ages provided).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables the development of noise-resilient voice communication, speech recognition, and biometrics in adverse environments (such as industrial and battlefield operations, emergency services, access control, and life-signal monitoring). Compliance with GDPR requirements (informed consent, anonymization, data encryption) was observed to protect participant privacy.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is restricted to the French language. The participant age distribution is skewed toward younger adults (median age 25, mean age 28.55). Physical variations in participant ear canal anatomies caused variance in acoustic sealing for in-ear sensors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Inadequate acoustic sealing occurs for certain ear canal anatomies when using rigid or soft in-ear microphones without custom molds; body-conduction sensors have inherent bandwidth limitations (especially temple and throat pickups); speech-noisy subset lacks paired clean reference recordings.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of machine learning models for speech enhancement (bandwidth extension and denoising), speech-to-phonemes recognition (ASR), speaker verification, physiological monitoring (such as heart rate tracking), and voice commands.
